scope_note: Corrective last-resort modeling pass for Apple Prineville. Five narrow, unallocated syntheses now survive: a same-land-account tax-payment break-even identity; a 2018 campus/company payroll sensitivity anchored to the reported 100 jobs and three official BLS Central Oregon occupation benchmarks; FY2025 campus electricity-cost sensitivity using EIA Oregon customer-class averages after PacifiCorp direct-access tariffs proved noncomputable from public inputs; deterministic FY2025 average-load conversion; and an EPA eGRID location-based electricity-emissions factor sensitivity. None is allocated to IM3 building 00397914434. The cost range is not Apple's bill, the payroll range is not observed payroll, and the emissions range is not Apple's market-based Scope 2 result and preserves Apple's 100 percent renewable-electricity claim. Investment, construction, supplier, community, net-fiscal and causal county-outcome candidates remain rejected for missing scope-compatible inputs or identification.

sources.title: Central Oregon nonmetropolitan area — May 2018 Occupational Employment and Wage Estimates
sources.notes: Official all-industry area table reports annual mean wages of $43,720 for all occupations, $77,300 for computer and mathematical occupations, and $118,000 for computer and information systems managers. These are scenario anchors, not Apple wages or an observed occupation mix.

sources.title: May 2018 OES county links to metropolitan and nonmetropolitan area pages
sources.notes: Official BLS crosswalk places Crook County in the Central Oregon nonmetropolitan area for the May 2018 wage table.

sources.title: Electric Power Monthly, February 2026 — Table 5.6.B
sources.notes: Table 5.6.B reports Oregon year-to-date through December average prices of 8.28 cents/kWh for industrial customers and 10.56 cents/kWh for commercial customers in 2025, versus 8.05 cents/kWh for industrial customers in 2024. These are statewide class averages, not Apple rates.

sources.title: Direct Access
sources.notes: Oregon PUC explains that a direct-access customer's local provider supplies distribution while a certified electricity service supplier supplies generation and transmission. The page establishes why a public utility tariff alone cannot reveal Apple's total energy cost.

sources.title: Oregon Schedule 748 — Large General Service 1,000 kW and Over, Direct Access Delivery Service
sources.notes: Effective January 1, 2025. Schedule 748 shows that direct-access delivery billing varies by delivery voltage, basic and facilities charges, facility capacity, on-peak demand, reactive power, Schedule 90 adjustments, metering and contract conditions; it does not disclose Apple's ESS energy price.

sources.title: Advice 24-002 / Docket UE 434 — 2025 Transition Adjustment Mechanism
sources.notes: Official filing page identifies the 2025 Transition Adjustment Mechanism and its supporting testimony. Together with Schedules 294-296, it confirms that transition treatment depends on direct-access election type, enrollment vintage, voltage and time period; Apple's election and enrollment vintage are not public.

sources.title: eGRID2023 Summary Tables, Revision 2
sources.notes: EPA reports total-output CO2e rates of 635.267 lb/MWh for the NWPP/WECC Northwest subregion and 365.0 lb/MWh for Oregon state generation. The model treats these as geographic-factor sensitivity anchors, not Apple's contractual or market-based emissions.

estimates.label: Tax-year 2025 same-account public-service-cost break-even threshold

period.label: Tax year 2025 account 19494 payment break-even threshold

scope.label: Apple Inc. Crook County land account 19494, tax lot 151607-00-00102, across the same local taxing recipients

interval.interpretation: The threshold equals the exact posted 2025 payment by definition; it is not an estimate of actual public-service cost, all-Apple tax contribution, recipient revenue or net fiscal impact.

parameters.name: same_account_property_tax_payment

provenance.detail: Posted tax-year 2025 payment, receipt 444833, for account 19494

parameters.transformation: Used unchanged as the equal-cost threshold for the same land account and tax year

estimates.confidence_rationale: The payment and threshold identity are exact for account 19494, while recipient distribution and actual same-scope marginal service costs are unavailable.
estimates.decision_relevance: States the annual public-cost level that would equal the latest verified single-account payment without inventing a service cost or fiscal surplus.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Marginal fire, police, road, water, wastewater, administrative, infrastructure and financing costs assigned to account 19494's recipients and tax year; recipient distributions and the other Apple accounts

derivation.formula: same-account annual public-service cost at break-even = posted tax-year 2025 payment = $31,334.07
assumptions: The threshold is an identity, not an observed or estimated public cost.
The hypothetical cost threshold uses the same land-account and tax-year scope as the posted payment.
No other Apple tax account, company-level billed total, abatement, fee, SDC or infrastructure amount is added or netted.

limitations: This is not an estimate of actual public-service cost.
Account 19494 is one 96.90-acre Apple land account with no improvements, not the selected building or all Apple property in Crook County.
The payment is not disaggregated among taxing recipients.
No positive or negative net fiscal result is asserted.
estimates.notes: Conditional same-account threshold only. It duplicates the payment numerically by design and must not be summed with the underlying tax claim.

estimates.label: 2018 campus/company annual payroll sensitivity for the reported 100 jobs

period.label: May/December 2018 wage and reported-jobs anchor year

scope.label: Apple Prineville data-center campus/company workforce represented by the joint release's 100-job statement

interval.interpretation: The same 100 reported jobs are valued at the May 2018 Central Oregon annual mean wage for all occupations, computer and mathematical occupations, and computer and information systems managers. This is occupation-composition sensitivity, not observed payroll, a true-value bound or a confidence interval.

parameters.name: reported_campus_jobs

provenance.detail: Joint City/Apple release says the data center created 100 jobs

parameters.transformation: Multiplied by each annual wage benchmark

provenance.detail: May 2018 Central Oregon all-occupations annual mean wage
May 2018 Central Oregon computer and mathematical occupations annual mean wage
May 2018 Central Oregon computer and information systems managers annual mean wage

estimates.confidence_rationale: The job count and same-vintage local wage benchmarks are public, but the release does not define FTE status, direct versus contractor employment, occupation mix, compensation, observation date or whether all 100 jobs persisted for a full year.
estimates.decision_relevance: Provides a transparent payroll scale for scenario testing while keeping every missing employment and occupation assumption visible.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Apple and contractor payroll records, dated direct and contract FTE, occupation mix, hours, benefits, tenure, worker residence and selected-building allocation

derivation.formula: 100 reported jobs × annual mean wage benchmark
assumptions: The reported 100 jobs are held constant across scenarios and treated as one full-year job equivalent each solely to express annual payroll scale.
Low, central and high apply three alternative occupation benchmarks to all 100 jobs; they do not assert an actual staffing mix.
Wages exclude benefits, payroll taxes, bonuses, stock compensation, overtime and contractor margin.
Crook County is represented by the official 2018 Central Oregon nonmetropolitan area.

limitations: The underlying job statement does not distinguish Apple employees, contractors, FTEs, vacancies or job-years.
Applying a single occupation group to every job is intentionally stylized and the endpoints are not bounds.
No worker-residence or local household-income effect is inferred.
The campus/company result cannot be assigned to the selected 9,228-square-foot building.
estimates.notes: Scenario only; do not present as realized Apple payroll, local payroll, labor income, compensation or an indirect/induced contribution.

This is a public-rate benchmark sensitivity, not Apple's tariff calculation, ESS contract price, utility bill, true-value bound or confidence interval.

provenance.detail: Apple-reported FY2025 Prineville campus electricity use
EIA 2024 Oregon industrial average price of 8.05 cents/kWh
EIA 2025 Oregon industrial average price of 8.28 cents/kWh

parameters.name: high_oregon_2025_commercial_price

provenance.detail: EIA 2025 Oregon commercial average price of 10.56 cents/kWh

parameters.transformation: Produces the high service-class benchmark scenario

estimates.confidence_rationale: Electricity use is directly reported and arithmetic is exact, but statewide class averages do not represent Apple's direct-access generation/transmission contract or its demand- and voltage-dependent delivery charges.
estimates.decision_relevance: Provides an auditable operating-cost scale and exposes service-class sensitivity after public tariff review showed that Apple's actual bill cannot be reconstructed.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Apple utility bills and ESS contract price; delivery voltage; meter count; facility capacity; monthly peak and reactive demand; on/off-peak use; Schedule 90, transition, credit and tax adjustments; fiscal/calendar alignment

assumptions: EIA statewide customer-class averages are used only as benchmark prices, not as Apple tariff rates.
Apple FY2025 consumption is paired with calendar-year 2024-2025 price anchors despite period mismatch.
No demand, reactive-power, fixed, transition, adjustment, tax, credit, renewable-contract or supplier charge is separately added.
The commercial average is a high service-class sensitivity, not evidence that Apple is billed as a commercial customer.

limitations: Apple is identified as a PacifiCorp direct-access customer, so its confidential ESS price and tariff configuration can differ materially from EIA statewide averages.
Schedule 748 cannot be calculated without delivery voltage, facility capacity, demand, reactive power, adjustments, meter and contract data.
The envelope is not a bound on Apple's actual bill.
The campus result cannot be assigned to the selected building and must not be treated as local retained spending.
estimates.notes: Benchmark cost sensitivity only. The separate deterministic average-load conversion is not an additional consumption estimate and neither result should be summed with the reported kWh.

estimates.label: FY2025 campus average electric load conversion

scope.label: Apple Prineville data-center campus electricity use; no selected-building or meter allocation

interval.interpretation: Deterministic conversion of reported annual energy divided by 8,760 hours. It is annual average load, not peak demand, nameplate capacity, contracted capacity or a tariff billing determinant.

parameters.name: fy2025_campus_electricity

provenance.detail: Apple-reported FY2025 Prineville campus electricity use

parameters.transformation: Divided by annual hours and 1,000 kW/MW

parameters.name: annual_hours

provenance.detail: Non-leap-year annualization for the FY2025 energy total

parameters.transformation: Converts annual energy to annual-average power

estimates.confidence_rationale: The conversion is deterministic from a directly reported campus energy total, but the source is rounded to millions of kWh and does not provide interval load or peak demand.
estimates.decision_relevance: Expresses the observed annual energy scale in average megawatts without substituting average load for capacity or peak demand.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Interval-metered load, monthly peak demand, contracted and nameplate capacity, meter count, redundancy configuration and selected-building allocation

assumptions: The reported campus energy total is used as published and is not allocated among meters, buildings or IT versus cooling loads.

limitations: Average load can be far below or above individual interval loads and cannot determine demand charges.
The input is rounded in Apple's facility table.
The result is campus wide and unallocated to the selected building.
It is a unit conversion, not an independent resource contribution.
estimates.notes: Conversion only; do not add to the kWh observation or interpret 30.48 MW as peak, capacity, incremental grid load or renewable-project output.

estimates.label: FY2025 campus location-based electricity-emissions factor sensitivity

period.label: Apple fiscal year 2025 electricity with EPA eGRID2023 geographic factors

scope.label: Apple Prineville data-center campus purchased-electricity consumption; no selected-building allocation

interval.interpretation: Low applies EPA's Oregon state-generation total-output CO2e rate; central/high apply EPA's NWPP/WECC Northwest subregion total-output CO2e rate. This is geographic-factor sensitivity for location-based context, not a statistical interval, avoided-emissions claim, marginal-emissions estimate or Apple's market-based Scope 2 result.

parameters.name: fy2025_campus_electricity

provenance.detail: Apple-reported 267 million kWh converted to 267,000 MWh

parameters.transformation: Multiplied by each total-output CO2e rate

provenance.detail: EPA eGRID2023 Oregon state total-output CO2e rate

parameters.name: central_nwpp_output_co2e_rate

provenance.detail: EPA eGRID2023 NWPP/WECC Northwest total-output CO2e rate

parameters.transformation: Produces the central and high geographic-factor scenario

parameters.name: pounds_per_metric_ton

provenance.detail: Exact mass-unit conversion used for reporting

parameters.transformation: Converts pounds CO2e to metric tons CO2e

estimates.confidence_rationale: The energy input and EPA factors are public, but the factor vintage predates FY2025, Oregon production and NWPP consumption-region factors differ substantially, and no source reconciles them to Apple's contractual instruments or reporting boundary.
estimates.decision_relevance: Shows the order of magnitude and geographic-factor sensitivity of grid-average location-based emissions while keeping Apple's renewable procurement claim separate.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Apple site-level location- and market-based Scope 2 inventory; contractual instrument attributes and retirement; hourly generation matching; utility loss treatment; exact eGRID subregion confirmation for every meter; FY2025 grid factor

derivation.formula: 267,000 MWh × eGRID total-output lb CO2e/MWh ÷ 2,204.62262185 lb/metric ton
assumptions: Oregon state output and NWPP subregion total-output rates are alternative location-based geographic benchmarks.

The NWPP factor is used as the central value because regional grid-average factors are more appropriate to consumption context than a state production factor; the Oregon factor is retained only to expose geographic-factor sensitivity.
No grid-loss uplift, marginal/non-baseload factor, avoided-emissions credit or renewable-contract adjustment is applied.
Apple's 100 percent renewable-electricity statement is a market/procurement claim and is not overwritten by this location-based sensitivity.

limitations: The range is driven by factor choice and is not a true-value bound.
eGRID2023 factors do not match Apple FY2025 exactly.
This is not an audited GHG Protocol inventory and must not be reported as Apple's Scope 2 emissions.
The model does not contradict or quantify Apple's separately reported 100 percent renewable-electricity procurement claim.
The campus result cannot be allocated to the selected building.
estimates.notes: Location-based grid-average sensitivity only. Central equals high because no more emissions-intensive location-based total-output factor was defensible; the non-baseload factor was rejected as a marginal rather than location-based accounting measure.
